root_cause.text: The driver manually frees a Wake-on-LAN IRQ with free_irq() that was allocated using devm_request_irq(), causing a double free when the devres framework automatically frees it again during device removal or probe failure.
root_cause.evidence: The patch removes bcmasp_wol_irq_destroy() which calls free_irq(priv->wol_irq, priv), and removes all calls to it from bcmasp_probe() error path and bcmasp_remove(), because the IRQ was requested with devm_request_irq() and devres will handle freeing it.

candidates.rationale: Manually frees an IRQ that was allocated with devm_request_irq(), causing a double free when devres automatically frees it again.
Condition guard that enables the vulnerable free_irq() call; without this check the double free might still occur if the IRQ number is valid.
Defines the function that contains the manual free_irq(), which is the vehicle for the double-free vulnerability.
Calls the vulnerable function in the error cleanup path, triggering a double free when the probe fails and devres later frees the IRQ.

vuln_statements.explanation: Directly frees an IRQ that was allocated with devm_request_irq. This causes a double free when the devres framework automatically frees it again during device removal or probe failure.
Condition that enables the manual free_irq() call. Without this check, the double free might still occur if the IRQ number is valid; the condition is part of the vulnerable code path.

Call to the vulnerable function in the error cleanup path of probe. Triggers a double free when the probe fails and devres later frees the IRQ.
Call to the vulnerable function during device removal. Causes a double free since devres will also free the IRQ automatically.
